symptom: PC in VLAN 10 cannot ping Server in VLAN 20. Gateway router subinterfaces are configured.

show_outputs.show running-config interface g0/0/0.10:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0.10
 encapsulation dot1Q 10
 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
!

diagnosis.fault_summary: Missing 802.1Q encapsulation on router subinterface G0/0/0.20
diagnosis.root_cause: Subinterface GigabitEthernet0/0/0.20 has an IP address assigned but lacks 'encapsulation dot1Q 20'. Without encapsulation, the router cannot tag or process incoming 802.1Q tagged frames from VLAN 20.
evidence_citations: G0/0/0.20 running-config shows 'ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0' without an encapsulation dot1Q statement.
diagnosis.remediation_cli_script:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0.20
 encapsulation dot1Q 20
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown

symptom: LAN hosts can ping 8.8.8.8 but domain name lookups (google.com) fail.

show_outputs.show access-lists 101:
Extended IP access list 101
 10 permit tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq www
 20 permit tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 443
 30 deny ip any any (120 matches)

diagnosis.fault_summary: Inbound Extended ACL 101 is dropping DNS queries due to missing UDP/TCP port 53 permit rule
diagnosis.root_cause: DNS queries use UDP port 53. ACL 101 permits only HTTP (80) and HTTPS (443); all other traffic hits the explicit 'deny ip any any' at line 30.
evidence_citations: ACL 101 permits only eq www and eq 443; no permit statement for UDP port 53 exists.
Line 30 'deny ip any any' has 120 matching dropped packets.
diagnosis.remediation_cli_script:
ip access-list extended 101
 25 permit udp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq domain
 26 permit tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq domain

symptom: OSPF neighbor state stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE between R1 and R2.

show_outputs.show ip ospf neighbor: Neighbor ID 2.2.2.2 Pri 1 State EXSTART/ - Dead Time 00:00:35 Address 10.0.0.2 GigabitEthernet0/0

diagnosis.fault_summary: OSPF adjacency stuck in EXSTART due to interface MTU size mismatch
diagnosis.root_cause: R1 has an MTU of 1500 bytes while R2 has an MTU of 1400 bytes. During the Database Description (DBD) packet exchange, R2 drops R1's oversized DBD packets, preventing transition to FULL.
evidence_citations: R1 MTU is 1500 bytes while R2 MTU is 1400 bytes on GigabitEthernet0/0.
